stem:
Divya spills a little water on a polished steel plate and the same amount on dry garden soil. After some time both wet patches look smaller.

What best explains the disappearing water?

options.text: On steel the water mainly evaporates; on soil it can both seep in and evaporate.
On steel the water must have seeped into the metal, just as it seeps into soil.
Neither case involves evaporation because no white mist or cloud was visible.
Water that seeps into soil turns into water vapour inside the soil as soon as it goes below the surface.

teacher.key_rationale: Impermeable steel blocks seepage, so drying there is evaporation; soil allows both. Mist is not required to call evaporation; seepage keeps water liquid below the surface.
